items.title: Strong spectral commutation of self-adjoint operators
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Setting.** Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral theorem. Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ and $B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$
with domains $D(A)$ and $D(B)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). By the spectral
theorem each of them has a unique spectral projection-valued measure on the
Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]); write $E_{A}$
for the spectral projection-valued measure of $A$ and $E_{B}$ for that of $B$.

**(b) Strong spectral commutation.** The operators $A$ and $B$ **strongly
commute**, or are **spectrally compatible**, when their spectral
projection-valued measures commute on every pair of Borel sets:
$$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)\qquad\text{for all Borel }\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is the relation that the term "compatible sharp observables" abbreviates
on the physical pages of the category. It is a condition on the two families
of projections, not on a single vector or on a formal difference of operator
products.

**(c) Not to be confused with a commutator identity on a core.** Let $D$ be a
linear subspace of $D(A)\cap D(B)$ with $A D\subseteq D$, $B D\subseteq D$. The
formal identity $ABu-BAu=0$ for every $u\in D$ is a different condition: it
constrains the two products on $D$ only, whereas clause (b) constrains the
spectral projections of $A$ and $B$ on all of $H$. The two conditions coincide
for bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, but for unbounded
operators neither one implies the other in general; a pair of self-adjoint
extensions of one symmetric operator whose difference is invisible on a dense
core is a standard witness. Clause (b), not the core identity, is the relation
that governs joint sharp outcomes and the vanishing of suitably formed
products; the examples page of the category records a domain-sensitive
counterexample.

**(d) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) fix a definition and a comparison of
conditions. They assert no physical claim, no joint measurement, no
simultaneous sharp value and no dynamical statement. All further content about
strong spectral commutation used by the category -- the bounded-calculus
consequences, the joint projection-valued measure criterion and the physical
readings -- is established as separate results with their own hypotheses.

## Remarks

- **Why projections and not commutators.** For unbounded $A$ and $B$ the
  products $AB$ and $BA$ may be defined on different domains, so the
  expression $AB-BA$ need not be an operator at all; the spectral projections
  $E_{A}(\Lambda)$ and $E_{B}(\Sigma)$ are bounded everywhere-defined
  projections, so their products are always defined and clause (b) makes
  literal sense. This is why the definition is stated at the level of the
  projection-valued measures.
- **Symmetric role of the two operators.** Clause (b) is manifestly symmetric
  in $A$ and $B$; the notation $E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)$
  is a single condition on each pair of Borel sets, not two conditions.

items.title: The Schroedinger-Robertson bound in anticommutator form and the Robertson bound on product domains
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A,B$ be symmetric
densely defined operators on $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$
with $\|u\|=1$ satisfy in addition $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$Bu\in D(A)$ and $Au\in D(B)$. Put
$$a:=\langle Au,u\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle Bu,u\rangle,\qquad x:=(A-a)u,\qquad y:=(B-b)u,\qquad \Delta A:=\|x\|,\qquad \Delta B:=\|y\|,$$
and write $\{A,B\}u:=ABu+BAu$ and $[A,B]u:=ABu-BAu$ for the pairings at $u$.
Then:

(a) $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $x,y\in H$, and
$$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab, \qquad \langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle ;$$

(b) *(Robertson bound)* $\Delta A\,\Delta B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|$;

(c) *(Schroedinger-Robertson bound)*
$$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
that is, with the expanded anticommutator pairing
$(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge\bigl(\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle\bigr|^{2}$;

(d) equality holds in (c) if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent;
in particular the Robertson bound (b) follows from (c) because the first
square is nonnegative;

(e) if $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then
the product-domain hypothesis $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ holds for every unit
$u\in H$ and clauses (a)-(d) apply to every unit $u$.

No energy-time inequality and no apparatus statement is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice; a complex Hilbert space $H$; symmetric densely defined $A,B$; a unit $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$ with $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$; the numbers $a,b$ and vectors $x,y$.

[F1] **Covariance-refined uncertainty.** For symmetric densely defined $A,B$ and a unit $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, with $a,b,x,y$ as above: $a,b$ are real and $x,y\in H$; $\operatorname{Cov}_{u}(A,B):=\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle$ is real and symmetric; the refined bound $(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge[\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}+[\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}$ holds, with equality if and only if $x,y$ are linearly dependent; and if $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ then $\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle$ and $(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge[\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}+\tfrac14|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle|^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-covariance-refined-uncertainty]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F2] **Commutator pairing.** If $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ then $([A,B]u,u)=\langle ABu,u\rangle-\langle BAu,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle Au,Bu\rangle$, and $\langle x,y\rangle=\langle Au,Bu\rangle-ab$ with real $a,b$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-weak-form-robertson-uncertainty]] clauses (a) and (c)).

[F3] **Inner products and Cauchy-Schwarz.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $|z|^{2}=(\operatorname{Re}z)^{2}+(\operatorname{Im}z)^{2}$, and $\|v\|\,\|w\|\ge|\langle v,w\rangle|$ with equality if and only if $v,w$ are linearly dependent ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]).

[F4] **Bounded operators.** A bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ has domain $H$, so for bounded self-adjoint $A,B$ the hypotheses $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$ and $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$ hold for every $u\in H$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** expand the two pairings of the centered vectors in terms of the anticommutator and commutator pairings using symmetry of the operators, then read the Schroedinger-Robertson inequality off the refined Cauchy-Schwarz bound.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Means and centered vectors] By [F1] the numbers $a$ and $b$ are real and $x=(A-a)u$, $y=(B-b)u$ lie in $H$, so $\Delta A=\|x\|$ and $\Delta B=\|y\|$ are the norms of the centered vectors. [given, F1]

2.1 [The real part is the anticommutator pairing] Since $Bu\in D(A)$ and $Au\in D(B)$, symmetry of $A$ gives $\langle ABu,u\rangle=\langle Bu,Au\rangle=\overline{\langle Au,Bu\rangle}$ and symmetry of $B$ gives $\langle BAu,u\rangle=\langle Au,Bu\rangle$. Adding, $\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle=2\operatorname{Re}\langle Au,Bu\rangle$. By [F2], $\langle x,y\rangle=\langle Au,Bu\rangle-ab$ with $ab\in\mathbb R$, hence $\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=\operatorname{Re}\langle Au,Bu\rangle-ab=\tfrac12\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-ab$. Expanding the anticommutator of the centered operators, using $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and $\langle Au,u\rangle=a$, $\langle Bu,u\rangle=b$, gives $\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\rangle=\langle\{A,B\}u,u\rangle-2ab$, so the two displays for the real part agree. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [The imaginary part is the commutator pairing] By [F2], $\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle Au,Bu\rangle$; by step 2.1 and [F2], $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=\operatorname{Im}\langle Au,Bu\rangle$, so $\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle$. This completes (a). [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [The two bounds] By [F1] the refined bound $(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge[\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}+[\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}$ holds. Substituting step 2.1 and $|\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle|=\tfrac12|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle|$ from step 3.1 gives (c); dropping the nonnegative first square gives (b). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F1, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Equality] By [F1] equality in the refined bound holds if and only if $x,y$ are linearly dependent; this is (d). [step 4.1, F1]

6.1 [Bounded case] If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators then $D(A)=D(B)=H$ and all products are everywhere defined, so the product-domain hypothesis of the statement holds for every unit $u\in H$ by [F4]; the displays of (a)-(d) are then unconditional in $u$. This is (e). [given, F4] ∎

items.title: Preparation variance and spread of an assigned sharp observable
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

## Remarks

- **Vanishing spread and eigenstates.** For a pure preparation of a unit
  vector $\psi\in D(A)$, clause (c) shows $\Delta_{\psi}A=0$ exactly when
  $A\psi=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle\psi$, that is exactly when $\psi$ is an
  eigenvector of $A$; this is the framework's reading of the textbook
  statement that the uncertainty of an observable vanishes in an eigenstate.
  The identification of a laboratory state with such a preparation is again a
  tested identification, not a consequence of the definition.
- **The product is not a joint distribution.** Clause (d) forms a product of
  two spreads of the same preparation; it does not introduce a joint outcome
  law of $A$ and $B$, and the product can be defined even when no joint sharp
  observable of the pair exists. Joint sharp observables are a separate
  notion with its own criterion.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Section 1, printed pages 1-3: the uncertainty defined as the norm of the centered vector and the identity (Delta A)^2 = <A^2> - <A>^2
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 3.1, printed pages 88-95 (PDF pages 100-107): expectation values and moments of a self-adjoint operator in a state

items.physical_scope: The reading of preparation variance and preparation spread for an assigned sharp observable of the framework: the variance and standard deviation of the outcome law of a preparation, their units, their existence hypotheses through the moment theorem, the centered-vector form for pure preparations of domain vectors, and the resulting definition of the product of two spreads. The item fixes terminology and readings of P1 and P2 only; it asserts no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance, no joint measurement, no dynamics and no empirical result, and it does not claim that any preparation has finite moments automatically.

items.title: Bounded Borel calculus of strongly commuting self-adjoint operators
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space and let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$ that strongly commute in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b):
$$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)\qquad\text{for all Borel }\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
For a bounded Borel function $h$ write $h(A):=\int h\,dE_{A}$ and
$h(B):=\int h\,dE_{B}$ for its operators under the bounded Borel functional
calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Then:

(a) for all bounded Borel $f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$,
$$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A);$$

(b) for every bounded Borel $f$ one has $f(B)D(A)\subseteq D(A)$, and
$$A\,f(B)x=f(B)Ax\qquad\text{for every }x\in D(A);$$
the same statement holds with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged, and it is
also true with $f(B)$ replaced by any bounded linear combination or norm limit
of bounded Borel functions of $B$;

(c) for every bounded Borel $f$ the bounded operator $f(B)$ commutes with all
spectral projections of $A$: $f(B)E_{A}(\Lambda)=E_{A}(\Lambda)f(B)$ for every
Borel $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R$. Consequently, for real-valued bounded Borel
$f$ the pair $(f(A),B)$ strongly commutes: the map
$F(\Lambda):=E_{A}(f^{-1}(\Lambda))$ is a projection-valued measure on the
Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ representing the bounded self-adjoint operator
$f(A)$, and $F(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)F(\Lambda)$ for all Borel
$\Lambda,\Sigma$; hence also $(f(A),g(B))$ strongly commutes for real-valued
bounded Borel $f,g$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; self-adjoint operators $A,B$ with strongly commuting spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$; bounded Borel functions $f,g,h$; vectors $x\in D(A)$ and $y\in D(B)$.

[F1] **Bounded Borel calculus.** For bounded Borel $h$ the operator $\Phi_{E}(h)=\int h\,dE$ is the unique bounded operator with $\langle\Phi_{E}(h)x,y\rangle=\int h\,dE_{x,y}$, it satisfies $\|\Phi_{E}(h)\|\le\|h\|_{\infty}$, $\langle\Phi_{E}(h)x,x\rangle=\int h\,dE_{x}$ and $\|\Phi_{E}(h)x\|^{2}=\int|h|^{2}\,dE_{x}$, it is the norm limit of $\int s_{n}\,dE$ for every sequence of complex simple functions with $\|h-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$, and for a simple function $s=\sum_{j}c_{j}\mathbf 1_{D_{j}}$ over a disjoint measurable cover one has $\int s\,dE=\sum_{j}c_{j}E(D_{j})$ ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clauses 1 and 2). A projection-valued measure is multiplicative, $E(\Lambda\cap\Sigma)=E(\Lambda)E(\Sigma)$, and every value is an orthogonal projection ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F2] **Star homomorphism.** The map $h\mapsto\Phi_{E}(h)$ is linear and unital, multiplicative, and adjoint preserving: $\Phi_{E}(hg)=\Phi_{E}(h)\Phi_{E}(g)$ and $\Phi_{E}(\overline h)=\Phi_{E}(h)^{*}$ ([[thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism]] clauses 1-3).

[F3] **Spectral theorem and truncated integrals.** The spectral projection-valued measure of a self-adjoint operator is unique, its scalar measures $E_{A,x}(\Lambda)=\langle E_{A}(\Lambda)x,x\rangle$ are finite Borel measures with $E_{A,x}(\mathbb R)=\|x\|^{2}$, and $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ with $\|Ax\|^{2}=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}$ for $x\in D(A)$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). For $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ Borel the operator $g(A)$ has domain $\{x:\int|g|^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and satisfies $\|g(A)x\|^{2}=\int|g|^{2}\,dE_{A,x}$; the operators $A_{n}:=\int\lambda\mathbf 1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}\,dE_{A}$ are bounded with $\|A_{n}x\|^{2}=\int\lambda^{2}\mathbf 1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}\,dE_{A,x}$, and $A_{n}x\to Ax$ for every $x\in D(A)$ ([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]]; [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] for the bounded truncations).

[F4] **Norm convergence of simple approximants.** For every bounded Borel function $h$ on $\mathbb R$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a complex simple Borel function $s$ with $\|h-s\|_{\infty}\le\varepsilon$: choose $M\ge\|h\|_{\infty}$ and split $[-M,M]$ into finitely many Borel sets of diameter at most $\varepsilon$, such as the preimages of intervals of length $\varepsilon$ and of the two unbounded tails; taking $s$ constant on each preimage at the value of a chosen point of that preimage gives the claim ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]] fixes the sigma-algebra on which the preimages are taken). Then $\|\Phi_{E}(h)-\Phi_{E}(s)\|\le\|h-s\|_{\infty}$ by [F1].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** verify the commutation on simple functions, transfer it to all bounded Borel functions by uniform approximation in operator norm, and control the domain statement by truncating the unbounded operator.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Simple functions commute] Let $f=\sum_{i}a_{i}\mathbf 1_{\Lambda_{i}}$ and $g=\sum_{j}b_{j}\mathbf 1_{\Sigma_{j}}$ be complex simple Borel functions over disjoint measurable covers. By [F1], $f(A)=\sum_{i}a_{i}E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})$ and $g(B)=\sum_{j}b_{j}E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})$, so $$f(A)g(B)=\sum_{i,j}a_{i}b_{j}E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})=\sum_{i,j}a_{i}b_{j}E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})=g(B)f(A),$$ because products of scalars commute and each pair of projections commutes by the strong commutation hypothesis. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 [Uniform approximation] Let $f,g$ be bounded Borel and fix $\varepsilon>0$. By [F4] choose simple $s,t$ with $\|f-s\|_{\infty}\le\varepsilon$ and $\|g-t\|_{\infty}\le\varepsilon$. By [F1], $\|s(A)-f(A)\|\le\varepsilon$, $\|t(B)-g(B)\|\le\varepsilon$ and $\|t(B)\|\le\|g\|_{\infty}+\varepsilon$, so the operator norm estimate $$\|s(A)t(B)-f(A)g(B)\|\le\|s(A)-f(A)\|\,\|t(B)\|+\|f(A)\|\,\|t(B)-g(B)\|\le\varepsilon\bigl(\|g\|_{\infty}+\varepsilon+\|f\|_{\infty}\bigr)$$ gives $s(A)t(B)\to f(A)g(B)$ in operator norm as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, with the approximants chosen along any sequence $\varepsilon_{n}\to0$. [F1, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (a)] Let $f,g$ be bounded Borel and choose the approximating sequences $s_{n}\to f$, $t_{n}\to g$ of step 1.2. By step 1.1, $s_{n}(A)t_{n}(B)=t_{n}(B)s_{n}(A)$ for every $n$; both sides converge in operator norm to $f(A)g(B)$ and to $g(B)f(A)$ respectively by step 1.2 (applied to the pairs $(s_{n},t_{n})$ and $(t_{n},s_{n})$). Limits in operator norm are unique, so $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$. This is (a). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (c), first part] Let $f$ be bounded Borel and let $\Lambda$ be Borel. Applying (a), already proved, to the pair $(f,\mathbf 1_{\Lambda})$ gives $f(B)E_{A}(\Lambda)=E_{A}(\Lambda)f(B)$. This is the first assertion of (c). [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (b), membership in the domain] Fix a bounded Borel $f$ and $x\in D(A)$; put $y:=f(B)x$. Put $u_{n}(\lambda):=\lambda\mathbf 1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}$, so that $A_{n}=\int u_{n}\,dE_{A}$ is a bounded Borel function of $A$; clause (a), already proved, applied to the pair of bounded Borel functions $(u_{n},f)$ gives $A_{n}f(B)=f(B)A_{n}$, so by [F1] and [F3] $$\int\lambda^{2}\mathbf 1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}\,dE_{A,y}=\|A_{n}y\|^{2}=\|A_{n}f(B)x\|^{2}=\|f(B)A_{n}x\|^{2}\le\|f(B)\|^{2}\|A_{n}x\|^{2}\le\|f(B)\|^{2}\|Ax\|^{2},$$ where the last step uses $\|A_{n}x\|\le\|Ax\|$ for $x\in D(A)$. Letting $n\to\infty$ and using monotone convergence on the left (equivalently the identities of [F3]) gives $\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,y}\le\|f(B)\|^{2}\|Ax\|^{2}<\infty$, so $y\in D(A)$. [step 3.1, F1, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Clause (b), action] With $x$ and $y=f(B)x$ as in step 4.1, both $x$ and $y$ lie in $D(A)$. By [F3], $A_{n}x\to Ax$ and $A_{n}y\to Ay$. Using $A_{n}f(B)=f(B)A_{n}$ from step 4.1, $$Ay=\lim_{n}A_{n}y=\lim_{n}A_{n}f(B)x=\lim_{n}f(B)A_{n}x=f(B)Ax,$$ the last equality because $f(B)$ is bounded and $A_{n}x\to Ax$. Hence $Af(B)x=f(B)Ax$ for every $x\in D(A)$. The exchange of roles follows because the strong commutation hypothesis is symmetric in $A$ and $B$, and the extension to bounded linear combinations and norm limits of bounded Borel functions of $B$ follows from linearity and norm continuity of operator multiplication. This proves (b). [step 4.1, F1, F3, algebra]

6.1 [Clause (c), composition] Let $f$ be real-valued and bounded Borel and put $F(\Lambda):=E_{A}(f^{-1}(\Lambda))$ for Borel $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R$. Preimages preserve the empty set, the whole space, complements and countable unions, so $F$ is a projection-valued measure. For a complex simple $u=\sum_{i}c_{i}\mathbf 1_{D_{i}}$ the preimages $f^{-1}(D_{i})$ are pairwise disjoint, so $\int u\,dF=\sum_{i}c_{i}F(D_{i})=\sum_{i}c_{i}E_{A}(f^{-1}(D_{i}))=\int(u\circ f)\,dE_{A}$; both sides extend to bounded Borel $u$ by the uniform approximation of [F1] and [F4], giving, for every $x\in H$, the scalar identity $\int u\,dF_{x}=\int(u\circ f)\,dE_{A,x}$. Taking $u=u_{n}$ from step 4.1 and letting $n\to\infty$ with monotone convergence gives $\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{x}=\int f^{2}\,dE_{A,x}=\|f(A)x\|^{2}<\infty$, where the last equality is [F1] for the bounded $f$; and the signed version of the same change of variables gives $\int\lambda\,dF_{x,y}=\int f\,dE_{A,x,y}=\langle f(A)x,y\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$. Since $f$ is real-valued, the adjoint-preservation clause of [F2] gives $f(A)^{*}=\Phi_{E_{A}}(\overline f)=\Phi_{E_{A}}(f)=f(A)$, so $f(A)$ is self-adjoint, and $f(A)$ is bounded by [F1]. By the uniqueness of the spectral projection-valued measure of a self-adjoint operator in [F3], $F$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the bounded self-adjoint operator $f(A)$. By the strong commutation hypothesis, $F(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{A}(f^{-1}(\Lambda))E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(f^{-1}(\Lambda))=E_{B}(\Sigma)F(\Lambda)$, so $(f(A),B)$ strongly commutes. Applying the same argument once more, now to the pair $(f(A),B)$ and the real-valued bounded Borel function $g$, shows that $(f(A),g(B))$ strongly commutes. This completes (c). [step 3.1, step 4.1, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: Strong spectral commutation, joint projection-valued measures and bounded Borel calculus
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space and let $A,B$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $A$ and $B$ strongly commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b), that is
$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)$ for all Borel
$\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(ii) there is a regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ whose values on measurable rectangles
([[def-measurable-rectangle]]) are
$G(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)$, and whose marginals are
$G(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda)$ and
$G(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)$;

(iii) $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel functions
$f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$, where the operators are those of the bounded
Borel functional calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

If these conditions hold, the projection-valued measure $G$ of (ii) is unique,
and for all bounded Borel $f,g$ one has the representation
$$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}f(a)g(b)\,dG(a,b).$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; self-adjoint operators $A,B$ on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$; Borel sets $\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$; bounded Borel functions $f,g$ on $\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Strong commutation.** $A$ and $B$ strongly commute exactly when $E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)$ for all Borel $\Lambda,\Sigma$, and this is a symmetric condition in $A$ and $B$ ([[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Bounded calculus of strongly commuting operators.** If $A,B$ strongly commute, then $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$ ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-bounded-borel-calculus-of-commuting-operators]] clause (a)).

[F3] **Joint projection-valued measure construction.** Let $E,F$ be regular projection-valued measures on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R$ with $E(B)F(C)=F(C)E(B)$ for all Borel $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$. Then there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ with $G(B\times C)=E(B)F(C)$ for every measurable rectangle $B\times C$, and its marginals are $G(B\times\mathbb R)=E(B)$ and $G(\mathbb R\times C)=F(C)$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-joint-pvm-construction]]).

[F4] **Regularity of spectral measures.** For every $x\in H$ the set function $E_{A,x}(\Lambda)=\langle E_{A}(\Lambda)x,x\rangle$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with $E_{A,x}(\mathbb R)=\|x\|^{2}$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). Every Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ that is finite on compact sets is regular, because $\mathbb R$ is locally compact Hausdorff and each of its open subsets is sigma-compact ([[thm-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular-when-open-sets-are-sigma-compact]]); hence $E_{A}$ and $E_{B}$ are regular projection-valued measures.

[F5] **Multiplicativity of projection-valued measures.** A projection-valued measure $G$ satisfies $G(S\cap T)=G(S)G(T)$ for all measurable $S,T$, and every value is an orthogonal projection ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F6] **Bounded integral and star homomorphism.** For a projection-valued measure $E$ on a measurable space and bounded measurable $h$, the operator $\Phi_{E}(h)=\int h\,dE$ satisfies $\|\Phi_{E}(h)\|\le\|h\|_{\infty}$ and is the norm limit of the integrals of uniformly convergent simple approximants; the map $h\mapsto\Phi_{E}(h)$ is linear, unital, multiplicative and adjoint preserving ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clauses 1 and 2, [[thm-pvm-integral-is-a-star-homomorphism]] clauses 1-3).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** prove the equivalence in the order (i) implies (ii) implies (i), (i) implies (iii), (iii) implies (i); obtain the representation of the last display from the unique joint projection-valued measure by simple approximation.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [(i) implies (ii)] Assume (i). By [F4] the projection-valued measures $E_{A}$ and $E_{B}$ are regular, and by [F1] they commute on all Borel pairs; so [F3] supplies a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$ with $G(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)$ for all measurable rectangles and with the stated marginals. This is (ii), including uniqueness. [given, F1, F3, F4]

1.2 [(ii) implies (i)] Assume (ii). For Borel $\Lambda,\Sigma$, the multiplicativity [F5] and the marginals give $$E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=G(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)\,G(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=G(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=G(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)\,G(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda),$$ using $(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)\cap(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=\Lambda\times\Sigma$. This is (i). [given, F5]

1.3 [(i) implies (iii)] This is [F2] verbatim. [given, F2]

1.4 [(iii) implies (i)] Assume (iii). Taking $f=\mathbf 1_{\Lambda}$ and $g=\mathbf 1_{\Sigma}$, which are bounded Borel, gives $E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)E_{A}(\Lambda)$. This is (i). [given, F6]

2.1 [The joint representation] Assume (i)-(iii) and let $G$ be the unique joint projection-valued measure of (ii), so that $G(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)$ for rectangles. Let $W(h):=\int h\,dG$ denote the bounded integral against $G$ for bounded Borel $h:\mathbb R^{2}\to\mathbb C$. For simple $s=\sum_{i}c_{i}\mathbf 1_{\Lambda_{i}}$, $t=\sum_{j}d_{j}\mathbf 1_{\Sigma_{j}}$ over disjoint covers of $\mathbb R$, the disjointness of the rectangles $\Lambda_{i}\times\Sigma_{j}$ and the defining property of the simple integral against a projection-valued measure give $$s(A)t(B)=\sum_{i,j}c_{i}d_{j}E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})=\sum_{i,j}c_{i}d_{j}G(\Lambda_{i}\times\Sigma_{j})=W(s\otimes t).$$ For general bounded Borel $f,g$ choose simple $s_{n},t_{n}$ with $\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$ and $\|g-t_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$ (uniform approximation by preimages of a shrinking partition of a bounded interval); then $\|s_{n}\otimes t_{n}-f\otimes g\|_{\infty}\to0$, so by the norm bound of [F6] both $s_{n}(A)t_{n}(B)\to f(A)g(B)$ and $W(s_{n}\otimes t_{n})\to W(f\otimes g)$ in operator norm, whence $f(A)g(B)=W(f\otimes g)=\int f(a)g(b)\,dG(a,b)$; combining with [F2] gives the displayed chain. [given, step 1.1, F2, F5, F6, construct, algebra] ∎

items.title: The position-momentum commutator identity on the product domain
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space with the componentwise position and momentum operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clauses (a) and (b), with domains
$$D(Q_{j})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},\qquad D(P_{k})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},$$
and let $D_{k}$ denote the weak partial derivative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then:

(a) *Product rule.* If $f\in H^{(r)}$ has $x_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ (the latter read
componentwise), then $x_{j}f$ lies in $D(P_{j})$ and
$$D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f;$$

(b) *The product domain.* $D(Q_{j}P_{j})=\{f\in D(P_{j}):\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$
and $D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f\in D(Q_{j}):\ D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$,
and their intersection is
$$D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{j}f,\ x_{j}f,\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\};$$

(c) *Commutator identity.* For every $f\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$,
$$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,f;$$

(d) *Core.* The componentwise Schwartz class
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
is contained in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, and (c) holds on it.

No identity of unbounded products is asserted outside $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$;
in particular no identity is asserted on $D(P_{j})$ alone.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; integers $d,r\ge1$; $\hbar>0$; the componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ with the displayed domains; a class $f\in H^{(r)}$; a coordinate index $j$.

[F1] **Domains and actions.** $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are self-adjoint with the maximal componentwise domains displayed in the Statement, $(Q_{j}f)_{l}=x_{j}f_{l}$ and $(P_{k}f)_{l}=-i\hbar D_{k}f_{l}$ componentwise, and $D(P_{k})=\{f:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}\}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (a), (b)). Hence, for a class $f$, the products $Q_{j}P_{j}f$ and $P_{j}Q_{j}f$ are defined exactly by the memberships $P_{j}f\in D(Q_{j})$ and $Q_{j}f\in D(P_{j})$ respectively, that is $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}$ and $D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}$ in the componentwise reading; no other hypothesis enters the definitions of the product domains.

[F2] **Weak Leibniz rule with a smooth factor.** Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ be open, $\eta\in C^{\infty}(\Omega;\mathbb C)$, and $u\in L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb C)$; suppose $u$ has weak derivatives $D^{\gamma}u\in L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ for all $\gamma\le\alpha$. Then $\eta u$ has a weak $\alpha$-derivative, and its almost-everywhere class is $D^{\alpha}(\eta u)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}(D^{\beta}\eta)D^{\alpha-\beta}u$ ([[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]). With $\alpha=e_{j}$ and $\eta(x)=x_{j}$ this gives $D_{j}(x_{j}u)=u+x_{j}D_{j}u$ in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for every $u\in L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ whose weak $j$-derivative exists in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$.

[F3] **Componentwise reading and Schwartz core.** Weak differentiation, multiplication by $x_{j}$ and the $L^{2}$ condition are read componentwise; a class lies in $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ exactly when all of its components lie in the scalar Schwartz class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); the Schwartz class is contained in $D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$, is mapped into itself by $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$, and satisfies the canonical commutation relation $(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar f$ there ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a) and (d)).

[F4] **Local square-integrability.** $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ componentwise, by the Cauchy-Schwarz bound on bounded measurable sets ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** apply the weak Leibniz rule with the smooth factor $x_{j}$ componentwise, read the product domains off the definitions, and assemble the commutator with the two actions.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [The product rule] Let $f\in H^{(r)}$ with $x_{j}f\in L^{2}$ and $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}$. Componentwise, each $f_{l}\in L^{2}\subseteq L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ has weak derivative $D_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\subseteq L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ by [F4], so [F2] with $\alpha=e_{j}$ and $\eta=x_{j}$ applies and gives $D_{j}(x_{j}f_{l})=f_{l}+x_{j}D_{j}f_{l}$ in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for every $l$. The right-hand side is a component of an $L^{2}$ class by hypothesis, so $D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}$ componentwise and $x_{j}f\in D(P_{j})$ with the displayed identity. This is (a). [given, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [The two product domains] By [F1], $D(Q_{j}P_{j})=\{f:\ P_{j}f\in D(Q_{j})\}=\{f\in D(P_{j}):\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}\}$ and $D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f:\ Q_{j}f\in D(P_{j})\}=\{f\in D(Q_{j}):\ D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}\}$, which are the first two displays of (b). For the intersection, the inclusion $\subseteq$ is immediate from these displays; conversely, if $f\in H^{(r)}$ has $D_{j}f$, $x_{j}f$ and $x_{j}D_{j}f$ in $L^{2}$, then $f\in D(P_{j})\cap D(Q_{j})$ and step 1.1 gives $D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}$, so $f$ lies in both product domains. This is (b). [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [The commutator] Let $f\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$. By [F1] and step 2.1, $(Q_{j}P_{j}f)_{l}=x_{j}(-i\hbar D_{j}f_{l})=-i\hbar\,x_{j}D_{j}f_{l}$ componentwise, while $(P_{j}Q_{j}f)_{l}=-i\hbar D_{j}(x_{j}f_{l})=-i\hbar(f_{l}+x_{j}D_{j}f_{l})$ by step 1.1. Subtracting componentwise, $((Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f)_{l}=-i\hbar x_{j}D_{j}f_{l}+i\hbar f_{l}+i\hbar x_{j}D_{j}f_{l}=i\hbar f_{l}$, so $(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar f$. This is (c). [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 [The core] Every component of a Schwartz class lies in the scalar Schwartz class, which is closed under multiplication by $x_{j}$ and under $D_{j}$ and is contained in $L^{2}$; hence $D_{j}f$, $x_{j}f$ and $x_{j}D_{j}f$ are in $L^{2}$, and step 2.1 places $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ in the intersection. The identity of (c), together with [F3], gives (d). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3] ∎

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (PDF pages 67-70): position and momentum operators, dense domains and the canonical commutation relation
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.3.1-2.3.2, printed pages 26-27 (PDF pages 34-35): the commutator [x,p]=i hbar computed on differentiable wavefunctions

items.title: Approximation of Q-P graph-domain vectors by product-domain vectors
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, and let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ with $\psi\ne0$ be a class and let
$D_{P}:=D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ be the product domain characterized in
[[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clause (b). Then
there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})_{n\ge1}\subseteq D_{P}$ with
$$\varphi_{n}\to\frac{\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{Q_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{P_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad \|\varphi_{n}\|=1$$
in $H^{(r)}$. In particular, if $\psi$ is a unit vector, then
$\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and
$P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in norm, and consequently
$$\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|,\qquad \langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|P_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|P_{j}\psi\| .$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; integers $d,r\ge1$; $\hbar>0$; the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ with their maximal componentwise domains; a class $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ with $\psi\ne0$.

[F1] **Componentwise operators and weak Leibniz.** $Q_{j}f=x_{j}f$ and $P_{j}f=-i\hbar D_{j}f$ componentwise on their maximal domains, and $D(P_{j})=\{f:\ \xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}\}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). For every smooth $\eta$ and every $u\in L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ whose weak $j$-derivative lies in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, one has $D_{j}(\eta u)=(D_{j}\eta)u+\eta D_{j}u$ in $L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ ([[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]).

[F2] **Cutoffs.** There is $\chi\in C^{\infty}_{c}(\mathbb R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi=1$ on $[-1,1]$, $\chi=0$ outside $[-2,2]$; for $\chi_{n}(t):=\chi(t/n)$ and $n\ge1$ one has $\chi_{n}=1$ on $[-n,n]$, $\chi_{n}=0$ outside $[-2n,2n]$, $\|\chi_{n}\|_{\infty}\le1$, and $\sup_{t}|t\chi_{n}'(t)|=\sup_{s}|s\chi'(s)|=:C_{\chi}<\infty$ ([[lem-schwartz-cutoffs-from-the-standard-smooth-step]]).

[F3] **Dominated convergence.** If $g_{n}\to g$ pointwise and $|g_{n}|\le G$ with $\int G<\infty$, then $\int g_{n}\to\int g$ ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F4] **The product domain.** $D_{P}=\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{j}f,\ x_{j}f,\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$ and on $D_{P}$ the product rule $D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f$ holds ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F5] **Inner-product continuity.** The inner product and the norm of $H^{(r)}$ are continuous for norm convergence ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** cut the vector off in the $j$-th coordinate by a smooth cutoff with bounded logarithmic derivative, verify the product-domain memberships with the weak Leibniz rule, and pass to the limit by dominated convergence before normalizing.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The truncated vector] For $n\ge1$ put $\widetilde\varphi_{n}:=\chi_{n}(x_{j})\psi$, the componentwise product of the class $\psi$ with the bounded smooth function $\chi_{n}(x_{j})$. Since $|\chi_{n}|\le1$ and $\psi\in L^{2}$, the class $\widetilde\varphi_{n}\in H^{(r)}$ satisfies $\|\widetilde\varphi_{n}\|\le\|\psi\|$. [given, F2]

2.1 [Membership in the product domain] Since $\psi\in D(P_{j})$, [F1] with $\eta=\chi_{n}$ gives $D_{j}\widetilde\varphi_{n}=\chi_{n}'\psi+\chi_{n}D_{j}\psi$, a sum of two $L^{2}$ classes because $\chi_{n}'$ and $\chi_{n}$ are bounded; hence $\widetilde\varphi_{n}\in D(P_{j})$. Next $x_{j}D_{j}\widetilde\varphi_{n}=x_{j}\chi_{n}'\psi+x_{j}\chi_{n}D_{j}\psi$: the first summand is bounded in modulus by $C_{\chi}|\psi|$ pointwise by [F2], and the second by $2n|D_{j}\psi|$ because $|x_{j}\chi_{n}(x_{j})|\le2n$ on the support of $\chi_{n}$ and $D_{j}\psi\in L^{2}$ since $\psi\in D(P_{j})$; hence $x_{j}D_{j}\widetilde\varphi_{n}\in L^{2}$. Also $x_{j}\widetilde\varphi_{n}=x_{j}\chi_{n}\psi\in L^{2}$ because $|x_{j}\chi_{n}(x_{j})|\le2n$ is bounded. By [F4] the three memberships place $\widetilde\varphi_{n}$ in $D_{P}$. [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Convergence of the truncated sequence] As $n\to\infty$ one has $\chi_{n}(x_{j})\to1$, $\chi_{n}(x_{j})'\to0$ and $x_{j}\chi_{n}'(x_{j})\to0$ pointwise, with the uniform bounds $|\chi_{n}|\le1$, $|\chi_{n}'|\le\|\chi'\|_{\infty}/n$ and $|x_{j}\chi_{n}'|\le C_{\chi}$. Hence, by [F3] applied componentwise, $\widetilde\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $$Q_{j}\widetilde\varphi_{n}=x_{j}\chi_{n}\psi\to x_{j}\psi=Q_{j}\psi,\qquad P_{j}\widetilde\varphi_{n}=-i\hbar\bigl(\chi_{n}'\psi+\chi_{n}D_{j}\psi\bigr)\to-i\hbar D_{j}\psi=P_{j}\psi$$ in $H^{(r)}$, the first term of the momentum difference being dominated by $(\|\chi'\|_{\infty}/n)\|\psi\|$ and the second converging by [F3] with dominating class $|D_{j}\psi|$. In particular $\|\widetilde\varphi_{n}\|\to\|\psi\|>0$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Normalization] For $n$ large enough that $\widetilde\varphi_{n}\ne0$, put $\varphi_{n}:=\widetilde\varphi_{n}/\|\widetilde\varphi_{n}\|$. Since $D_{P}$ is a linear subspace by [F4], $\varphi_{n}\in D_{P}$, and $\|\varphi_{n}\|=1$. Dividing the convergences of step 2.2 by $\|\widetilde\varphi_{n}\|\to\|\psi\|$ gives $\varphi_{n}\to\psi/\|\psi\|$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi/\|\psi\|$ and $P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi/\|\psi\|$. If $\psi$ is a unit vector, these are the convergences $\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and $P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$. [step 2.2, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Means and second moments] Assume $\psi$ is a unit vector. By [F5], $\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|=\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}-0\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|$ from the convergence $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$; the same two limits hold with $Q_{j}$ replaced by $P_{j}$. This completes the statement. [step 3.1, F5, algebra] ∎

items.title: The Robertson relation for preparation spreads of assigned sharp observables
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with outcome laws $\mu^{A},\mu^{B}$ and let
$\Delta_{\rho}A,\Delta_{\rho}B$ be their preparation spreads in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let $\psi$ be a unit vector and
write $a:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, $b:=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$. Then:

(a) **Weak form.** If $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, then the means $a,b$ are real,
the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, both are read in
the units $u_{A}$ and $u_{B}$, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\bigl|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle\bigr| .$$

(b) **Robertson form.** If in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$B\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(B)$, then the pairing
$\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle:=\langle AB\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle BA\psi,\psi\rangle$
is defined, is purely imaginary, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr| ,$$
read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; moreover the anticommutator refinement
$$(\Delta_{\psi}A)^{2}(\Delta_{\psi}B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}\psi,\psi\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr|^{2}$$
holds, with equality in the refined bound if and only if $(A-a)\psi$ and
$(B-b)\psi$ are linearly dependent.

(c) **Bounded observables.** If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined
self-adjoint operators, then clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit
$\psi\in H$ with all hypotheses automatic ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

(d) **Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1
and P2 and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two outcome
laws in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law, no apparatus
resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, and no
time observable. In particular no energy-time inequality is asserted, and
clauses (a)-(c) do not claim that a laboratory procedure realizes either
observable or attains the bounds; whether a concrete preparation and apparatus
realize the pair $(A,u_{A})$ and produce the spread $\Delta_{\psi}A$ is a
tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1 and P2; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$, $(B,u_{B})$ with self-adjoint operators $A,B$ and declared units; a unit vector $\psi$; the preparation spreads of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]].

[F1] **Moments and spread.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ and a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$, the mean and the second moment of the outcome law exist with $m=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle\in\mathbb R$ and $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}=\|A\psi\|^{2}$, and the preparation spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F2] **Schroedinger-Robertson bound.** For symmetric densely defined $A,B$ and a unit $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$ with $u\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, with real means $a,b$ and centered vectors $x=(A-a)u$, $y=(B-b)u$, the refined bound and the equality clause hold: $(\Delta A)^{2}(\Delta B)^{2}\ge[\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}+[\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle]^{2}$, with equality if and only if $x,y$ are linearly dependent, and $\Delta A\Delta B\ge\tfrac12|\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle|$ with $\langle[A,B]u,u\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle$; and $\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=\tfrac12\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}u,u\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-schrodinger-robertson-anticommutator-bound]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F3] **Weak-form identification without products.** For symmetric densely defined $A,B$ and a unit $u\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, with real means $a,b$ and $x,y$ as above, $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=\operatorname{Im}\langle Au,Bu\rangle$ because $\langle x,y\rangle=\langle Au,Bu\rangle-ab$ with $ab\in\mathbb R$, and the refined Cauchy-Schwarz bound yields $\Delta A\Delta B\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle Au,Bu\rangle|$ ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-schrodinger-robertson-anticommutator-bound]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-weak-form-robertson-uncertainty]] clauses (a), (c)).

[F4] **Units.** The declared unit of an assigned sharp observable and the reading of powers and products of units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the commutator pairing $\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle$ and the product $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B$ are read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$ ([[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clause (d)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** instantiate the mathematical Schroedinger-Robertson bound at the two self-adjoint operators of the assigned observables and read the definitions of mean and spread from the moment theorem.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Weak form] Let $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$ be a unit vector. By [F1] the means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$ are real, the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, and they equal the norms of the centered vectors $x=(A-a)\psi$ and $y=(B-b)\psi$. By [F3], $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle$ and $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle|$, which is (a). [given, F1, F3]

2.1 [Robertson form] Assume in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$. Then $A,B$ satisfy the product-domain hypothesis of [F2] at $u=\psi$; combining the Robertson bound and the anticommutator refinement of [F2] with the identifications of [F1] gives the two displays of (b), and the equality clause transfers because the centered vectors there are exactly $(A-a)\psi$ and $(B-b)\psi$. The pairing $\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle$ is purely imaginary by [F2]. This is (b). [step 1.1, F1, F2]

3.1 [Bounded case] If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined self-adjoint operators, then $D(A)=D(B)=H$ and all products are everywhere defined, so the hypotheses of clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit $\psi\in H$; clauses (a) and (b) apply verbatim. This is (c). [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 [Units and scope] The units are those of [F4]; the preparation spread is the outcome-law spread of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] and no apparatus, disturbance, joint-law or time quantity enters steps 1.1-2.1, which is the scope statement (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F1, F4] ∎

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Section 2, printed pages 3-6: the uncertainty inequality (2.14), its commutator-anticommutator refinement (2.28) and the saturation conditions

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 3.1, printed pages 88-95 (PDF pages 100-107): expectation values, variances and spectral measures of self-adjoint operators

items.physical_scope: Conditional statements about the preparation spreads of two assigned sharp observables of the framework in a pure preparation of a unit vector: the weak Robertson bound Delta A Delta B >= |Im<A psi, B psi>| for unit vectors in both domains, the Robertson bound Delta A Delta B >= |<[A,B]psi,psi>|/2 and its anticommutator refinement when the product domains also contain the vector, and the automatic validity of these hypotheses for bounded observables. The statement is a conditional consequence of P1 and P2 and the cited mathematics; it concerns preparation spreads of outcome laws only, and asserts no apparatus error, no disturbance, no joint measurement, no energy-time inequality and no empirical result.

items.title: The position-momentum preparation relation of the massive spin-s model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the
internal-factor assignment P6 of the framework, read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q_{j},P_{j}$ be the model's $j$-th position and
$j$-th momentum operators with their maximal domains, and let
$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ be their preparation spreads in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and put
$$a:=\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad x:=(Q_{j}-a)\psi,\qquad y:=(P_{j}-b)\psi .$$
Then:

(a) $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ are defined and
$$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\,\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) if in addition $\psi\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, then
$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})\psi=i\hbar\psi$ and the bound of (a) follows from the
Robertson relation for the two observables;

(c) for every unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ the centered pairing has the
exact imaginary part
$$\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
consequently equality $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}=\hbar/2$ holds if
and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent and
$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the cited
mathematics. It concerns the two separately assigned position and momentum
outcome laws in one preparation, needs no hypothesis on the products
$Q_{j}P_{j}$ or $P_{j}Q_{j}$, and asserts no joint outcome law of position and
momentum (which does not exist; see the compatibility results of this page),
no apparatus realization, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and
no empirical result. Massless, relativistic, singular-potential and boundary
realizations are separate models for which no such relation is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5 and P6 read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of the model with their maximal domains; a unit vector $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$; the numbers $a,b$ and the centered vectors $x,y$.

[F1] **Model operators.** $Q_{j}$ and $P_{j}$ are the componentwise position and momentum operators of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a), self-adjoint with domains $D(Q_{j})=\{f:x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \forall l\}$ and $D(P_{j})=\{f:D_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \forall l\}$, and the model assigns to them the status of assigned sharp observables in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a) ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Moments and spreads.** For a unit vector in $D(Q_{j})$ the mean and variance of the position law exist with $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}=\|(Q_{j}-a)\psi\|$ where $a=\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle$ is real, and likewise for $P_{j}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a) and (b), [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F3] **Product domain and commutator.** $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f:D_{j}f,x_{j}f,x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}\}$ and on it $(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar f$ ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F4] **Approximation.** For every nonzero $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})$ of unit vectors in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ with $\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and $P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in $H_{s}$, and with $\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle$, $\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|$ and the analogous momentum limits ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-approximation-by-product-domain-vectors]]).

[F5] **Robertson relation.** For two assigned sharp observables and a unit vector in the intersection of the two operator domains and the two product domains, the spread product is at least half the absolute value of the commutator pairing ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] clause (b)).

[F6] **Cauchy-Schwarz and its equality case.** In a complex inner product space, $\|v\|\,\|w\|\ge|\langle v,w\rangle|\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle v,w\rangle|$ and $|\langle v,w\rangle|^{2}=(\operatorname{Re}\langle v,w\rangle)^{2}+(\operatorname{Im}\langle v,w\rangle)^{2}$, with equality in the first inequality if and only if $v,w$ are linearly dependent ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** prove the bound first on the product domain from the commutator identity and the Robertson relation, transfer it to the full maximal domain of the pair by the cutoff approximation, and compute the exact imaginary part of the centered pairing along the approximating sequence.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Product-domain case] Let $\varphi$ be a unit vector in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$. By [F1] the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ are the model's assigned sharp observables with their maximal domains, so the preparation spreads and the Robertson relation of [F5] apply to them. By [F3], $(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$, so $\langle[Q_{j},P_{j}]\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar\|\varphi\|^{2}=i\hbar$. By [F5] the product of the preparation spreads of the two assigned observables satisfies $\Delta_{\varphi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi}P_{j}\ge\tfrac12|i\hbar|=\hbar/2$. [given, F1, F3, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Approximation] Let $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and let $(\varphi_{n})$ be the approximating sequence of [F4]. For every $n$, $\varphi_{n}$ is a unit product-domain vector, so step 1.1 gives $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$. By [F2] and [F4], $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}^{2}=\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|^{2}-\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle^{2}\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|^{2}-\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}^{2}$, and the analogous identity holds for $P_{j}$ with the momentum limits of [F4]; taking square roots and products gives $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}P_{j}\to\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$. Hence the limit satisfies $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$, which is (a); and on the product domain the same computation together with [F3] is the derivation of (b). [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Exact imaginary part] Keep the notation of step 2.1 and put $a_{n}:=\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle$, $b_{n}:=\langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle$, $x_{n}:=(Q_{j}-a_{n})\varphi_{n}$, $y_{n}:=(P_{j}-b_{n})\varphi_{n}$. By [F3], $\langle[Q_{j},P_{j}]\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle=-2i\operatorname{Im}\langle x_{n},y_{n}\rangle$ for every $n$, hence $\operatorname{Im}\langle x_{n},y_{n}\rangle=\tfrac12 i\,\langle[Q_{j},P_{j}]\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle=\tfrac12 i\,(i\hbar)=-\hbar/2$. By [F4], $x_{n}\to x$ and $y_{n}\to y$ in $H_{s}$ (each is the sum of a convergent term and a scalar multiple of a convergent term), so the inner product is continuous and $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=\lim_{n}\operatorname{Im}\langle x_{n},y_{n}\rangle=-\hbar/2$. This is the first display of (c). [given, step 2.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Equality characterization] For a unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ put $\Delta_{Q}:=\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$, $\Delta_{P}:=\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$. By step 3.1, $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\hbar/2$, and by [F6] $$\hbar/2\le\Delta_{Q}\Delta_{P}=\|x\|\,\|y\|\ge|\langle x,y\rangle|\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle|=\hbar/2 .$$ Equality $\Delta_{Q}\Delta_{P}=\hbar/2$ holds exactly when both inequalities are equalities, that is (by the equality case of [F6] and the identity $|\langle x,y\rangle|^{2}=(\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle)^{2}+(\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle)^{2}$) when $x,y$ are linearly dependent and $\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$. This completes (c). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F6, algebra]

5.1 [Scope] Clauses (a)-(c) were obtained from the model's operators, the product-rule identity, the approximation lemma and the Robertson relation; no joint outcome law, apparatus, disturbance, dynamics or empirical input enters. This is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 3.4 and 3.4.1, printed pages 81-88 (PDF pages 84-91): canonical commutation relations, the position-momentum bound Delta x Delta p >= hbar/2 and the Gaussian saturation

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Section 2, printed pages 3-6: the uncertainty inequality for position and momentum and the conditions for saturation

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1 and Section 8.1, printed pages 55-58 and 173-175 (PDF pages 67-70 and 185-187): position and momentum as self-adjoint operators and the algebraic calculus behind the canonical commutation relation

items.physical_scope: The position-momentum preparation relation of the massive spin-s particle model of the framework, for one particle of mass parameter m>0 and spin label s: for every unit state vector in D(Q_j) cap D(P_j) the product of the preparation spreads of the j-th position and j-th momentum is at least hbar/2, with no product-domain hypothesis, together with the equality characterization by linear dependence of the centered vectors and the exact imaginary part -hbar/2. The statement is a conditional consequence of P2, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics; it concerns the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws and asserts no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no apparatus realisation, no disturbance and no empirical result.

items.title: Compatible sharp observables, their joint law and the ideal joint instrument
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the ideal
conditional measurement postulate P3 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Call a regular
projection-valued measure $H$ on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\mathbb R^{2}$ a
**joint sharp observable** of the pair when its marginals are the two spectral
measures,
$$H(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda),\qquad H(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)\qquad(\Lambda,\Sigma\ \text{Borel}),$$
and call the pair **compatible** when such an $H$ exists. Then:

(a) **Criterion.** The pair is compatible if and only if $A$ and $B$ strongly
commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b), if and only if
$f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$; the joint sharp observable
$H$ is then unique, and for bounded Borel $f,g$
$$f(A)g(B)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}f(a)g(b)\,dH(a,b) .$$

(b) **Joint outcome law.** If the pair is compatible, then for every
preparation $\rho$ the assignment
$$\mu^{H}_{\rho}(S):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,H(S)\bigr)\qquad(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{2}\ \text{Borel})$$
is a probability measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$, the **joint
outcome law** of the pair in $\rho$, and its marginals are the individual
laws:
$$\mu^{H}_{\rho}(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\Lambda),\qquad \mu^{H}_{\rho}(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=\mu^{B}_{\rho}(\Sigma) .$$
For the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ it reads
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}(S)=\|H(S)\psi\|^{2}$.

(c) **Ideal finite-resolution joint instrument.** If the pair is compatible
and $(P_{1},\dots,P_{n})$, $(Q_{1},\dots,Q_{m})$ are the projections of two
finite disjoint Borel partitions of $\mathbb R$,
$P_{i}:=E_{A}(\Lambda_{i})$, $Q_{j}:=E_{B}(\Sigma_{j})$ with
$\bigcup_{i}\Lambda_{i}=\bigcup_{j}\Sigma_{j}=\mathbb R$, then
$R_{ij}:=H(\Lambda_{i}\times\Sigma_{j})=P_{i}Q_{j}$ are mutually orthogonal
projections with strong sum $I$, and in the framework's declared ideal sharp
measurement of the family $(R_{ij})$ the outcome probabilities are
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$ with marginals $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{i})$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho Q_{j})$; the sequential declared ideal measurements
of $(P_{i})$ and then $(Q_{j})$ give the same joint law
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$, with order-independent conditional states,
and both update families are repeatable on the corresponding outcomes.

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and
the cited mathematics. A joint sharp observable, when it exists, is a
mathematical object of the framework: it supplies a joint outcome law, not an
apparatus. The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes the joint
measurement, with its resolution, losses and systematics, is a physical
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7. No disturbance statement, no dynamics and no empirical result is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P3 in the stated readings; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$, $(B,u_{B})$ with spectral projection-valued measures $E_{A},E_{B}$; Borel sets $\Lambda,\Sigma$; finite disjoint Borel partitions $(\Lambda_{i})$, $(\Sigma_{j})$ of $\mathbb R$; a preparation $\rho$; a unit vector $\psi$.

[F1] **Outcome law and its properties.** For an assigned sharp observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E$, the law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets, equals $\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}$ for the pure preparation of a unit vector, and is affine in the preparation ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Joint projection-valued measure criterion.** For self-adjoint $A,B$ the following are equivalent: strong spectral commutation of $E_{A}$ and $E_{B}$; existence of a unique regular projection-valued measure $H$ on $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^{2})$ with $H(\Lambda\times\Sigma)=E_{A}(\Lambda)E_{B}(\Sigma)$ and marginals $H(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=E_{A}(\Lambda)$, $H(\mathbb R\times\Sigma)=E_{B}(\Sigma)$; and $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$. In that case $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)=\int f(a)g(b)\,dH(a,b)$ for all bounded Borel $f,g$ ([[thm-nrqm-uncertainty-joint-pvm-criterion]]).

[F3] **Values of a projection-valued measure.** For a projection-valued measure $H$ the values $H(S)$ are orthogonal projections with $H(S\cap T)=H(S)H(T)$ and $H(\varnothing)=0$, $H(\mathbb R^{2})=I$, and $H$ is strongly finitely additive; in particular orthogonal projections with $\sum_{ij}R_{ij}=I$ in the strong sense form a declared ideal sharp measurement family of the framework ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a) and (b)).

[F4] **Compatible Lueders instruments.** Let $E,F$ be regular commuting projection-valued measures with joint projection-valued measure $G$, let $(B_{i})$, $(C_{j})$ be finite disjoint Borel families, and put $P_{i}:=E(B_{i})$, $Q_{j}:=F(C_{j})$, $R_{ij}:=P_{i}Q_{j}=G(B_{i}\times C_{j})$. Then the $R_{ij}$ are mutually orthogonal projections, the sequential declared ideal measurements of $(P_{i})$ and $(Q_{j})$ give the joint law $\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$ in either order with order-independent conditional states $\rho\mapsto R_{ij}\rho R_{ij}/\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$ when $\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})>0$, and the marginal sums reproduce the individual bin laws; the update is repeatable on the corresponding outcomes ([[lem-nrqm-composites-compatible-luders-repeatability]] clauses (a)-(e)).

[F5] **Bounded calculus comparison.** If $E_{A}$ and $E_{B}$ strongly commute, then $f(A)g(B)=g(B)f(A)$ for bounded Borel $f,g$ ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-bounded-borel-calculus-of-commuting-operators]] clause (a), [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** read the mathematical joint projection-valued measure criterion as the definition of compatibility, obtain the joint law from the scalar spectral measure of $H$, and instantiate the mathematical compatible Lueders instrument at the two spectral projection-valued measures.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Criterion] The definitions of a joint sharp observable and of compatibility in the Statement are exactly the conditions of [F2], and the bounded Borel calculus identity of [F2] is [F5]; hence the three conditions of (a) are equivalent and $H$ is unique with the stated representation. This is (a). [given, F2, F5]

2.1 [Joint law] Assume the pair is compatible and let $H$ be its joint sharp observable. For every preparation $\rho$, [F1] applied to the assigned sharp observable with projection-valued measure $H$ on $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^{2})$ shows that $\mu^{H}_{\rho}(S)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H(S))$ is a probability measure with the pure reading $\|H(S)\psi\|^{2}$. Its marginals are $\mu^{H}_{\rho}(\Lambda\times\mathbb R)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H(\Lambda\times\mathbb R))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\Lambda))=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\Lambda)$ and likewise for $B$, using the marginal property of $H$ from the Statement. This is (b). [step 1.1, F1]

2.2 [Ideal joint instrument] Assume compatibility and let $(P_{i})$, $(Q_{j})$ be as in (c). By [F3], $R_{ij}=H(\Lambda_{i}\times\Sigma_{j})$ are orthogonal projections with $R_{ij}=P_{i}Q_{j}=Q_{j}P_{i}$ and $\sum_{i,j}R_{ij}=H(\mathbb R^{2})=I$ in the strong sense; thus $(R_{ij})$ is a finite declared ideal sharp measurement family with outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho R_{ij})$. Applying [F4] with $E=E_{A}$, $F=E_{B}$ and the families $(\Lambda_{i})$, $(\Sigma_{j})$ gives the stated sequential agreement, order-independence of the conditional states, the marginal sums and repeatability. This is (c). [step 1.1, F3, F4]

3.1 [Scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 used only P1-P3 and the cited mathematics; no apparatus identification, disturbance, dynamics or empirical data entered, so (d) holds. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

items.title: Position and momentum of the massive model have no joint sharp observable
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment P6, read
for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a coordinate index $j$. Then:

(a) the spectral projection-valued measures $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$ of the
model's $j$-th position and $j$-th momentum do not strongly commute: there are
Borel sets $\Lambda,\Sigma\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$E_{Q_{j}}(\Lambda)E_{P_{j}}(\Sigma)\ne E_{P_{j}}(\Sigma)E_{Q_{j}}(\Lambda)$;

(b) consequently the pair $(Q_{j},P_{j})$ is not compatible: there is no regular
projection-valued measure $H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$ whose
marginals are $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$, and in particular the framework
assigns to the pair no joint sharp outcome law in any preparation;

(c) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5, P6 and the cited
mathematics and concerns the model's assigned sharp operators only. It does
not assert that no approximate or unsharp joint measurement exists, gives no
error-disturbance relation, and records no apparatus or empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P2, P5, P6 read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the model operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ with their maximal domains; real $t\ne0$; a nonzero class $\psi\in D(Q_{j})$.

[F1] **Model operators and translations.** $Q_{j}$ and $P_{j}$ are self-adjoint with the maximal componentwise domains $D(Q_{j})=\{f:x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \forall l\}$ and $D(P_{j})=\{f:D_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \forall l\}$, and the componentwise translation $T_{te_{j}}f=f(\cdot-te_{j})$ satisfies $T_{te_{j}}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{te_{j}}Q_{j}T_{te_{j}}^{-1}=Q_{j}-tI$ and $T_{te_{j}}=\exp\bigl(-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\bigr)$, the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of $P_{j}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (a), (c) and (d); [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Bounded Borel calculus.** If two self-adjoint operators $A,B$ have strongly commuting spectral projection-valued measures, then for every bounded Borel $f$ one has $f(B)D(A)\subseteq D(A)$ and $Af(B)x=f(B)Ax$ for every $x\in D(A)$ ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-bounded-borel-calculus-of-commuting-operators]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Joint sharp observable criterion.** A pair of assigned sharp observables is compatible -- possesses a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R^{2}$ with the two spectral measures as marginals -- exactly when the two spectral projection-valued measures strongly commute ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]] clause (a); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b)).

[F4] **The exponential function.** $\exp\bigl(-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}tp\bigr)$ is a bounded Borel function of $p\in\mathbb R$ with values of modulus $1$, so it is admissible in the bounded Borel functional calculus of a self-adjoint operator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** suppose the two projection-valued measures commute and use the bounded Borel calculus to make the unitary translation group of the momentum commute with the position operator, contradicting the conjugation identity $TQ_{j}T^{-1}=Q_{j}-tI$.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Supposition and its consequence] Assume for contradiction that $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$ strongly commute, and fix $t\ne0$. By [F4] the function $f(p)=\exp(-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}tp)$ is bounded Borel, and by [F1] its operator is $f(P_{j})=T_{te_{j}}$. Applying [F2] with $A=Q_{j}$, $B=P_{j}$ gives $T_{te_{j}}D(Q_{j})\subseteq D(Q_{j})$ and $$T_{te_{j}}Q_{j}\eta=Q_{j}T_{te_{j}}\eta\qquad\text{for every }\eta\in D(Q_{j}).$$ [given, assume-contra, F1, F2, F4]

2.1 [The contradiction] Let $\psi\in D(Q_{j})$ be nonzero, which exists because $D(Q_{j})$ is dense, and put $\eta:=T_{te_{j}}^{-1}\psi$; by the domain invariance of [F1], $\eta\in D(Q_{j})$. The conjugation identity of [F1] gives $$T_{te_{j}}Q_{j}\eta=(Q_{j}-tI)T_{te_{j}}\eta=(Q_{j}-tI)\psi,$$ while step 1.1 gives $T_{te_{j}}Q_{j}\eta=Q_{j}T_{te_{j}}\eta=Q_{j}\psi$. Hence $(Q_{j}-tI)\psi=Q_{j}\psi$, that is $t\psi=0$, which contradicts $\psi\ne0$ and $t\ne0$. Therefore $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$ do not strongly commute, and there are Borel sets on which the two projections fail to commute. This proves (a). [given, step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [No joint sharp observable] By [F3] a pair of assigned sharp observables is compatible exactly when its spectral projection-valued measures strongly commute; by step 2.1 this fails for $(Q_{j},P_{j})$, so no regular projection-valued measure on $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^{2})$ has $E_{Q_{j}}$ and $E_{P_{j}}$ as marginals, and no joint sharp outcome law of the pair is assigned by the framework to any preparation. This proves (b); the scope statement (c) records that no approximate or unsharp joint measurement, error-disturbance relation, apparatus model or empirical result is asserted by steps 1.1-2.1. [given, step 2.1, F3, discharge-contradiction] ∎
