B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', Sections 7-8, printed pages 16-19: simultaneous diagonalization of commuting Hermitian operators

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): the momentum operator as the generator of translations and the algebraic position-momentum calculus

items.title: What the uncertainty and compatibility page adopts, proves and does not claim
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**Adopted, not restated.** The physical content of this page is the state and
composition postulate P1 and the observable and probability postulate P2 in
the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] for the
position and momentum statements). The page adopts no further physical
assumption beyond the model postulates P5 and P6 used to name $Q_{j}$ and
$P_{j}$; the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem are carried explicitly
in every mathematical item.

**What is proved.** [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] fixes the
reading of preparation variance and spread.
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] proves the weak Robertson bound
for unit vectors in both domains, the Robertson bound and its anticommutator
refinement on the product domains, and the automatic validity for bounded
observables. [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]] proves
$\Delta Q_{j}\Delta P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$ on the full maximal domain of the pair,
with the exact imaginary part $-\hbar/2$ and the equality characterization.
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]],
[[thm-nrqm-uncertainty-joint-pvm-criterion]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]] fix
strong spectral commutation, prove its equivalence with the existence and
uniqueness of a joint sharp observable and give the joint law with its
marginals; [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-incompatible]] proves
that the model's position and momentum are incompatible. All of these are
conditional consequences of the postulates and the cited mathematics.

**What is not claimed.** No item of this page asserts an apparatus resolution,
a measurement error, a disturbance of the preparation, an approximate or
unsharp joint measurement, a joint position-momentum law, a time observable or
a universal energy-time inequality. The inequalities concern the spreads of
the outcome laws of one preparation; they are not statements about the
precision of a laboratory procedure, and the equalities of the position and
momentum item are properties of specific preparations, not of every state. The
identification of a preparation and an apparatus with the model's states and
operators is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation
and apparatus postulate P7; neither the postulates nor the theorems here
report a measured value, a trial count or a statistical inference. Agreement
of the conditional predictions with data would test the combined model and
apparatus assumptions; it is not established or claimed here.

**Distinctions preserved.** The page keeps preparation spread, apparatus
resolution and disturbance separate throughout; it also keeps the mathematical
identity $[A,B]u=0$ on a dense core separate from strong spectral commutation.
The examples companion records a domain-sensitive counterexample, the Gaussian
family that saturates the position-momentum bound, the spin-$\tfrac12$ spread
account, the energy-time scope remark and the error-disturbance distinction.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 5 'Uncertainty Principle and Compatible Observables', printed pages 1-19: uncertainty defined, the uncertainty inequality and its saturation conditions, the energy-time discussion with time as a parameter, and simultaneous diagonalization of commuting observables

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Sections 2.1, 3.1 and 8.1, printed pages 55-58, 87-100 and 173-175 (PDF pages 67-70, 99-112, 185-187): self-adjoint operators, spectral measures and generators of one-parameter groups

It proves nothing itself and reports no observation.

items.title: The Gaussian family attains the position-momentum bound in the massive model
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 and the massive-particle
model postulate P5 read through
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a spinless particle
($s=0$, $r=1$) of mass parameter $m>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Fix a width
$\sigma>0$ and define
$$\psi_{\sigma}(x):=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})},\qquad x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
with momentum width $\sigma_{p}:=\hbar/\sigma$ and momentum representative
$U\psi_{\sigma}$ under the model's momentum transform $U$. Then:

(i) $\psi_{\sigma}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ is a unit vector, so
its ray is a pure preparation; $\psi_{\sigma}\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all
$j,k$, and $P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=i\hbar\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$;

(ii) the position outcome law of $Q_{j}$ has density
$(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$ in the coordinate $t=x_{j}$,
with mean $0$ and variance $\sigma^{2}/2$, so
$\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}Q_{j}=\sigma/\sqrt2$;

(iii) $U\psi_{\sigma}=\psi_{\sigma_{p}}$, that is
$$(U\psi_{\sigma})(p)=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|p|^{2}/(2\sigma_{p}^{2})};$$
the momentum outcome law of $P_{k}$ has density
$(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-p_{k}^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$, with mean $0$ and
variance $\sigma_{p}^{2}/2=\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$, so
$\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}P_{k}=\hbar/(\sigma\sqrt2)$;

(iv) for every $j$,
$$\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}Q_{j}\,\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}P_{j}=\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
and the centered vectors are linearly dependent with vanishing real part of
their pairing:
$$Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\frac{i\sigma^{2}}{\hbar}P_{j}\psi_{\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{Re}\bigl\langle Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma},P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}\bigr\rangle=0,$$
so the equality case of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]] clause (c) is realized.

The computation is one family of preparations in the model; it is not a
characterization of all preparations attaining $\hbar/2$, involves no dynamics,
no detection model and no empirical value.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A width $\sigma>0$; the action constant $\hbar>0$; the model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with $r=1$; the vector $\psi_{\sigma}$; the momentum transform $U$; a coordinate $j$ or $k$.

[F1] **Heat kernel.** For $t>0$ the function $\Gamma(x,t)=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/(4t)}$ on $\mathbb R^{n}$ is in $C^{\infty}$, satisfies $\int_{\mathbb R^{n}}\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=1$ ([[def-heat-kernel]], [[lem-heat-kernel-normalisation-scaling-and-derivatives]]), and has absolutely integrable first and second moments with $\int_{\mathbb R^{n}}x_{i}\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=0$ and $\int_{\mathbb R^{n}}x_{i}x_{j}\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=2t\delta_{ij}$ ([[lem-first-and-second-moments-of-the-heat-kernel]]).

[F2] **Gaussian Fourier transform and momentum transform.** With the $2\pi$-normalized unitary Plancherel transform one has $\mathcal F_{2}(e^{-\pi t|x|^{2}})(\xi)=t^{-n/2}e^{-\pi|\xi|^{2}/t}$ for $t>0$ ([[lem-euclidean-gaussian-fourier-transform-with-two-pi-normalization]]); the model's momentum transform satisfies $U=D_{\hbar}\mathcal F_{2}$ with $D_{\hbar}g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}g(p/(2\pi\hbar))$ and $(U\varphi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\varphi(x)\,dx$ for $\varphi\in L^{1}\cap L^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clauses (a),(c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (a)).

[F3] **Outcome laws of the model.** For a unit class $\psi$ the position law of $Q_{j}$ is $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx$ and the momentum law of $P_{k}$ is $\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}|(U\psi)(p)|^{2}\,dp$ ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clauses (a) and (c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[F4] **Moments and spreads.** For a unit vector in the domain of the operator the mean and variance of the outcome law exist and equal the quadratic-form mean and the squared norm of the centered vector ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a) and (b), [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F5] **Position-momentum relation.** For every unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ one has $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$, with equality if and only if the centered vectors are linearly dependent and their pairing has vanishing real part ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]] clauses (a) and (c)).

[F6] **Schwartz classes and weak derivatives.** A class lies in $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ exactly when all seminorms $\sup_{x}|x^{\alpha}\partial^{\beta}f(x)|$ are finite; a $C^{1}$ function whose classical partial derivatives lie in $L^{2}$ has those derivatives as weak derivatives, and products of Schwartz classes with polynomials are again Schwartz classes ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]]).

[F7] **Product integration.** Integrals of nonnegative measurable functions on product spaces may be iterated ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]), and $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-u^{2}}du=\sqrt{\pi}$ ([[thm-gaussian-integral]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** identify $|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}$ with a heat-kernel slice so that normalisation and all moments come from the heat-kernel items, transform the Gaussian with the published Gaussian Fourier lemma and the model's normalisation, and read the equality case of the position-momentum relation from the explicit centered vectors.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [The preparation] With $t:=\sigma^{2}/4$ one has $(4\pi t)^{-3/2}=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/2}$ and $|x|^{2}/(4t)=|x|^{2}/\sigma^{2}$, so $|\psi_{\sigma}(x)|^{2}=\Gamma(x,\sigma^{2}/4)$; by [F1], $\|\psi_{\sigma}\|^{2}=\int\Gamma(x,\sigma^{2}/4)\,dx=1$. The function $\psi_{\sigma}$ is smooth and all of its polynomial-weighted derivatives are bounded because the exponential beats every polynomial, so $\psi_{\sigma}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ by [F6]. Its classical partial derivative is $\partial_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$, a Schwartz class, which by [F6] is its weak derivative $D_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$; hence $x_{j}\psi_{\sigma},D_{j}\psi_{\sigma}\in L^{2}$ and $\psi_{\sigma}\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ with $P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-i\hbar D_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=i\hbar\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$. This is (i). [given, F1, F6, algebra]

2.1 [Position law and spread] By [F3], [F7] and step 1.1, the law of $Q_{j}$ has density $$f_{j}(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi_{\sigma}(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}\,dx_{\perp}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi\sigma^{2}}}e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}} .$$ By [F1] the first moment of this density vanishes and its second moment equals the one-dimensional heat-kernel second moment $2\cdot(\sigma^{2}/4)=\sigma^{2}/2$, so by [F4] the mean is $0$ and the variance is $\sigma^{2}/2$; hence $\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}Q_{j}=\sigma/\sqrt2$. This is (ii). [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

2.2 [Momentum representative] Write $\psi_{\sigma}=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-\pi t_{0}|x|^{2}}$ with $t_{0}=1/(2\pi\sigma^{2})$. By [F2], $\mathcal F_{2}\psi_{\sigma}(\xi)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}t_{0}^{-3/2}e^{-\pi|\xi|^{2}/t_{0}}$, and substituting $t_{0}^{-3/2}=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{3/2}$ and $\pi/t_{0}=2\pi^{2}\sigma^{2}$ gives $\mathcal F_{2}\psi_{\sigma}(\xi)=2^{3/2}\pi^{3/4}\sigma^{3/2}e^{-2\pi^{2}\sigma^{2}|\xi|^{2}}$. By [F2], $U\psi_{\sigma}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\mathcal F_{2}\psi_{\sigma}(p/(2\pi\hbar))$; its coefficient is $(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}2^{3/2}\pi^{3/4}\sigma^{3/2}=(\sigma^{2}/(\pi\hbar^{2}))^{3/4}=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/4}$ and its exponent is $-2\pi^{2}\sigma^{2}|p|^{2}/(4\pi^{2}\hbar^{2})=-|p|^{2}/(2\sigma_{p}^{2})$ with $\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$. This is the displayed Gaussian $U\psi_{\sigma}=\psi_{\sigma_{p}}$. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Momentum law and spread] The momentum law density of $P_{k}$ is, by [F3] and step 2.2, the $k$-th marginal $(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-p_{k}^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$ of $|\psi_{\sigma_{p}}|^{2}$; by the same heat-kernel moment computation as in step 2.1 with $\sigma$ replaced by $\sigma_{p}$, its mean is $0$ and its variance is $\sigma_{p}^{2}/2=\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$, so $\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}P_{k}=\hbar/(\sigma\sqrt2)$. This is (iii). [step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Saturation and equality case] Multiplying the two spreads of steps 2.1 and 3.1 gives $\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi_{\sigma}}P_{j}=(\sigma/\sqrt2)(\hbar/(\sigma\sqrt2))=\hbar/2$, the lower bound of [F5]. The centered vectors are $Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma}-0=Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$ and $P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}-0=P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$ because both means vanish, and step 1.1 gives $Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\frac{i\sigma^{2}}{\hbar}\,P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$, a linear dependence; moreover $\langle Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma},P_{j}\psi_{\sigma}\rangle=\frac{i\hbar}{\sigma^{2}}\|Q_{j}\psi_{\sigma}\|^{2}$ is purely imaginary, so its real part vanishes. By the equality clause of [F5] these two properties are exactly the equality case of the position-momentum relation. This is (iv). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F4, F5, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **No converse is claimed.** The verification shows that the Gaussian family
  attains the bound and satisfies the equality conditions of
  [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]]; it does not claim that
  every preparation with $\Delta Q_{j}\Delta P_{j}=\hbar/2$ is Gaussian, and
  no classification of the equality set is recorded here.
- **One family, three coordinates.** The computation is uniform in the
  coordinate $j$ and in the width $\sigma$; different widths give different
  preparations, and the momentum width $\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$ is a property
  of this family in the model, not a measured resolution.

items.title: Spin one half: spread identity, incompatible component outcomes and saturated Robertson bounds
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment P6, read for the spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=\tfrac12$ and $r=2$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Write
$S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ for the model's internal-factor operators of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c), so that
$J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), and let
$\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}$ be the preparation spread of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Then, for every unit
$\psi\in H_{1/2}$:

(a) with $\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}:=\bigl(\langle S_{x}\psi,\psi\rangle,\langle S_{y}\psi,\psi\rangle,\langle S_{z}\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\sum_{i\in\{x,y,z\}}\bigl(\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\bigr)^{2}=\frac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}-\bigl|\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}\bigr|^{2}\ge\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2},$$
so at least one component satisfies
$\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\ge\hbar/\sqrt6$; in particular no unit state has all
three component spreads equal to zero;

(b) for every pair of distinct components the spectral projection-valued
measures fail to commute; explicitly, with
$P_{i}^{\pm}:=\tfrac12(I\pm\sigma_{i})$ the spectral projections of $S_{i}$ at
$\pm\hbar/2$,
$$P_{x}^{+}P_{y}^{+}-P_{y}^{+}P_{x}^{+}=\tfrac{i}{2}\sigma_{z}\ne0,$$
and cyclically; consequently no pair of the three components possesses a joint
sharp observable in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]];

(c) in the state $\psi=f\,e_{1/2}$ with any unit spatial factor
$f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and the basis vector
$e_{1/2}$ of the internal factor,
$$\langle S_{z}\rangle_{\psi}=\frac{\hbar}{2},\qquad \langle S_{x}\rangle_{\psi}=\langle S_{y}\rangle_{\psi}=0,\qquad \Delta_{\psi}S_{x}=\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\frac{\hbar}{2},\qquad \Delta_{\psi}S_{z}=0,$$
and $\Delta_{\psi}S_{x}\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\hbar^{2}/4=\tfrac12|\langle[S_{x},S_{y}]\psi,\psi\rangle|$,
so the Robertson bound of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] is attained in this state;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6
and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics. They concern the internal-factor
coupling constants of the model; they assert no laboratory measurement of a
spin component, no Stern-Gerlach apparatus model, no dynamics, no empirical
value and no interpretation of $S_{i}$ as a rotating body or as orbital
angular momentum.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5, P6 read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with $s=\tfrac12$; the internal operators $S_{i}$; a unit vector $\psi\in H_{1/2}$; a unit spatial factor $f$; the basis vector $e_{1/2}$.

[F1] **Internal operators.** $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ acts on the internal factor as the matrix action, $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$, and the Pauli matrices satisfy $\sigma_{i}^{2}=I$ and $\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_{k}$, so $S_{i}^{2}=\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{4}I$, $S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\tfrac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}I$ and $[S_{x},S_{y}]=i\hbar S_{z}=i\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2}\sigma_{z}$ ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c)).

[F2] **Spreads in the finite factor.** $S_{i}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so for every unit $\psi$ the mean $\langle S_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and the variance $(\Delta_{\psi}S_{i})^{2}=\langle S_{i}^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle S_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$ exist ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a) and (b), [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b) and (c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)).

[F3] **Spectral projections of the components.** For $\lambda=\pm\hbar/2$ the spectral projection $E_{S_{i}}(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto the eigenspace $\ker(S_{i}-\lambda)$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clause (a), [[def-projection-valued-measure]]); the matrices $P_{i}^{\pm}=\tfrac12(I\pm\sigma_{i})$ satisfy $P_{i}^{\pm}=P_{i}^{\pm\,2}=P_{i}^{\pm\,*}$, $P_{i}^{+}+P_{i}^{-}=I$ and $S_{i}P_{i}^{\pm}=\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}P_{i}^{\pm}$, so $P_{i}^{\pm}=E_{S_{i}}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})$ ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F4] **Cauchy-Schwarz for the vector mean.** For $g\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R^{3})$ one has $\bigl|\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}g(x)\,dx\bigr|\le\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|g(x)|\,dx$, and in $\mathbb C^{2}$ with the standard inner product $|\langle\sigma_{i}z,z\rangle|\le\|z\|^{2}$ for every $z\in\mathbb C^{2}$ (the pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the vectors $z$ and $\sigma_{i}z$, whose norms agree because $\sigma_{i}$ is unitary) ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]).

[F5] **Robertson relation.** For two assigned sharp observables and a unit vector in the intersection of the two operator domains and the two product domains, the spread product is at least half the absolute value of the commutator pairing; bounded observables satisfy the hypotheses automatically ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F6] **Compatibility criterion.** A pair of assigned sharp observables is compatible exactly when its spectral projection-valued measures strongly commute ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-compatible-sharp-observables-and-joint-law]] clause (a)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** evaluate the finite spin matrices pointwise on the internal factor, sum the three component variances, bound the vector mean by the Bloch identity, and read off the noncommutation of the spectral projections and the saturated Robertson bound in the $S_{z}$ eigenstate.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Spread identity] By [F1], $\sum_{i}S_{i}^{2}=\tfrac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}I$, so for a unit $\psi$, $$\sum_{i}\bigl(\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\bigr)^{2}=\sum_{i}\langle S_{i}^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\sum_{i}\langle S_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\frac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}-\bigl|\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}\bigr|^{2}$$ by [F2]. This is the identity of (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Noncommutation of the component projections] By [F3] the projections $P_{i}^{\pm}=E_{S_{i}}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})$ are the spectral projections of the components. Using $\sigma_{i}^{2}=I$ and $\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}=i\sigma_{z}$, $\sigma_{y}\sigma_{x}=-i\sigma_{z}$ from [F1], $$P_{x}^{+}P_{y}^{+}-P_{y}^{+}P_{x}^{+}=\tfrac14(\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}-\sigma_{y}\sigma_{x})=\tfrac14(2i\sigma_{z})=\tfrac{i}{2}\sigma_{z}\ne0,$$ because $\sigma_{z}e_{1/2}=e_{1/2}$. Cyclic permutations of the Pauli relations give the corresponding nonvanishing differences for the other two pairs. Hence the spectral projection-valued measures of every two distinct components fail to strongly commute, and by [F6] no pair of components possesses a joint sharp observable. This is (b). [given, F1, F3, F6, algebra]

2.1 [Bound on the vector mean] Choose a representative of the class $\psi$ and write $g(x):=\bigl(\langle\sigma_{x}\psi(x),\psi(x)\rangle,\langle\sigma_{y}\psi(x),\psi(x)\rangle,\langle\sigma_{z}\psi(x),\psi(x)\rangle\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}$, which is defined for almost every $x$ and measurable. For $z=(z_{1},z_{2})\in\mathbb C^{2}$ the Pauli relations of [F1] give $\langle\sigma_{x}z,z\rangle=2\operatorname{Re}(z_{1}\overline{z_{2}})$, $\langle\sigma_{y}z,z\rangle=-2\operatorname{Im}(z_{1}\overline{z_{2}})$ and $\langle\sigma_{z}z,z\rangle=|z_{1}|^{2}-|z_{2}|^{2}$, hence the Bloch identity $\sum_{i}\langle\sigma_{i}z,z\rangle^{2}=4|z_{1}z_{2}|^{2}+(|z_{1}|^{2}-|z_{2}|^{2})^{2}=\|z\|^{4}$; so $|g(x)|=\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{2}}^{2}$ for almost every $x$, and $g\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R^{3})$ with $\|g\|_{1}=\|\psi\|^{2}=1$; and $\langle S_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}g_{i}(x)\,dx$ because $S_{i}$ acts on the internal factor. By [F4], $$\bigl|\langle\mathbf S\rangle_{\psi}\bigr|=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl|\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}g(x)\,dx\Bigr|\le\frac{\hbar}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|g(x)|\,dx=\frac{\hbar}{2}.$$ Substituting into step 1.1 gives $\sum_{i}(\Delta_{\psi}S_{i})^{2}\ge\tfrac{3\hbar^{2}}{4}-\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{4}=\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2}$; since the sum of the three nonnegative numbers is at least $\hbar^{2}/2$, their maximum is at least $\hbar^{2}/6$, so some component satisfies $\Delta_{\psi}S_{i}\ge\hbar/\sqrt6$. This completes (a). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.2 [The $S_{z}$ eigenstate] Let $\psi=f\,e_{1/2}$ with $\|f\|=1$. Since $S_{i}$ acts on the internal factor, the pointwise expectations are constants: $\sigma_{z}e_{1/2}=e_{1/2}$ gives $\langle S_{z}\rangle_{\psi}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$, and $\sigma_{x}e_{1/2}=e_{-1/2}$, $\sigma_{y}e_{1/2}=ie_{-1/2}$ with the basis orthonormal give $\langle S_{x}\rangle_{\psi}=\langle S_{y}\rangle_{\psi}=0$. By [F1], $\langle S_{x}^{2}\rangle_{\psi}=\langle S_{y}^{2}\rangle_{\psi}=\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{4}$, so $\Delta_{\psi}S_{x}=\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}=\hbar/2$; and $S_{z}\psi=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\psi$ by the same eigenrelation, so $\Delta_{\psi}S_{z}=0$. Finally $[S_{x},S_{y}]=i\hbar S_{z}$ from [F1] gives $\tfrac12|\langle[S_{x},S_{y}]\psi,\psi\rangle|=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\langle S_{z}\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{4}=\Delta_{\psi}S_{x}\Delta_{\psi}S_{y}$, so the Robertson bound of [F5] is attained. This is (c). [step 1.2, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] Clauses (a)-(c) used the internal matrices, the spread definition, the spectral-projection criterion and the Robertson relation; no measurement procedure, apparatus, dynamics or empirical input entered, which is the scope statement (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2] ∎

items.title: A commutator vanishing on a dense core does not imply strong spectral commutation
items.statement:
## Statement refuted

Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space, let $A,B$ be self-adjoint
operators on $H$, and let $D\subseteq D(A)\cap D(B)$ be a dense linear
subspace with $AD\subseteq D(B)$ and $BD\subseteq D(A)$. If $ABu=BAu$ for
every $u\in D$, then the spectral projection-valued measures of $A$ and $B$
strongly commute in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] clause (b).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; the interval $(0,1)$; the twisted-periodic momentum operators $P_{0}$ and $P_{\pi}$ on $L^{2}(0,1;\mathbb C)$; the space $D:=C^{\infty}_{c}(0,1)$; the exponential functions $\varphi_{0}=1$ and $\psi_{0}(x)=e^{i\pi x}$.

[F1] **Twisted-periodic momentum.** For $0<L<\infty$ and $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ put $D_{\theta}:=\{u\in H^{1}(0,L):u^{*}(L)=e^{i\theta}u^{*}(0)\}$ and $P_{\theta}u:=-iDu$. Then $D_{\theta}$ is dense, $P_{\theta}$ is self-adjoint, the functions $\varphi_{n}(x)=L^{-1/2}e^{i(2\pi n+\theta)x/L}$ form a complete orthonormal family, $P_{\theta}\varphi_{n}=\kappa_{n}\varphi_{n}$ with $\kappa_{n}=(2\pi n+\theta)/L$, the eigenvalues are simple, and $\sigma(P_{\theta})=\{\kappa_{n}:n\in\mathbb Z\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-intervals-twisted-periodic-momentum-domain]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **The trace and integration by parts.** $H^{1}(0,L)$ consists of the classes with an $L^{2}$ weak derivative, each class has a continuous absolutely continuous representative $u^{*}$ with $\int_{0}^{L}u\overline{v'}=u^{*}(L)\overline{v^{*}(L)}-u^{*}(0)\overline{v^{*}(0)}-\int_{0}^{L}u'\overline v$ for $u,v\in H^{1}(0,L)$; a compactly supported smooth function vanishes near the endpoints, so $C^{\infty}_{c}(0,L)\subseteq D_{\theta}$ for every $\theta$ ([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]], [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F3] **Density.** $C^{\infty}_{c}(0,1)$ is dense in $L^{2}(0,1;\mathbb C)$ ([[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-ltwo-of-an-open-set]]).

[F4] **Atoms are eigenspace projections.** For a self-adjoint operator with spectral projection-valued measure $E$ and eigenvalue $\lambda$, the projection $E(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clause (a), [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

[F5] **The complex exponential and its integral.** The function $x\mapsto e^{i\alpha x}$ is differentiable with derivative $i\alpha e^{i\alpha x}$ ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]), and for a continuous function on an interval with a continuous primitive $G$ one has $\int_{a}^{b}G'=G(b)-G(a)$ ([[cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function]], applied to real and imaginary parts).

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** exhibit two distinct self-adjoint extensions of the same symmetric operator that agree on the dense core of test functions, so that the commutator vanishes there, and show by explicit eigenprojections that their spectral projection-valued measures fail to commute.

**Given:** The data of the refuted statement and [F1]-[F5]; take $H=L^{2}(0,1;\mathbb C)$, $A:=P_{0}$, $B:=P_{\pi}$, $D:=C^{\infty}_{c}(0,1)$.

1.1 [The hypothesis of the refuted statement holds] By [F2], $D\subseteq D_{0}\cap D_{\pi}=D(A)\cap D(B)$, and both operators act on $D$ by $u\mapsto-iDu$, which maps $D$ into itself; hence for $u\in D$ the products $ABu=-D^{2}u$ and $BAu=-D^{2}u$ are defined and $[A,B]u=0$. By [F3] the space $D$ is dense in $H$. So the hypotheses of the refuted statement are satisfied. [given, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Spectral data] Applying [F1] with $L=1$: $A=P_{0}$ has the complete orthonormal family $\varphi_{n}(x)=e^{2\pi inx}$ with simple eigenvalues $2\pi n$, and $B=P_{\pi}$ has the complete orthonormal family $\psi_{n}(x)=e^{i(2n+1)\pi x}$ with simple eigenvalues $(2n+1)\pi$, for $n\in\mathbb Z$. In particular $\varphi_{0}=1$ spans the eigenspace of $A$ at $0$ and $\psi_{0}(x)=e^{i\pi x}$ spans the eigenspace of $B$ at $\pi$. [given, F1]

2.1 [The two spectral projections] By [F4], $E_{A}(\{0\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{0}$, and $E_{B}(\{\pi\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb C\psi_{0}$. Since $\varphi_{0}=1$ is a unit vector, $E_{A}(\{0\})u=\langle u,\varphi_{0}\rangle\varphi_{0}$; since $\|\psi_{0}\|^{2}=\int_{0}^{1}|e^{i\pi x}|^{2}dx=1$, likewise $E_{B}(\{\pi\})u=\langle u,\psi_{0}\rangle\psi_{0}$. [step 1.2, F1, F4, algebra]

2.2 [The inner products] By [F5], $\int_{0}^{1}e^{-i\pi x}dx=\bigl[e^{-i\pi x}/(-i\pi)\bigr]_{0}^{1}=(e^{-i\pi}-1)/(-i\pi)=2/(i\pi)=-2i/\pi$, and by conjugation $\int_{0}^{1}e^{i\pi x}dx=2i/\pi$. Hence $\langle\varphi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle=-2i/\pi$ and $\langle\psi_{0},\varphi_{0}\rangle=2i/\pi$. [step 1.2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Noncommutation] With $u:=\varphi_{0}=1$ and the projections of step 2.1, $$E_{B}(\{\pi\})u=\langle u,\psi_{0}\rangle\psi_{0}=-\frac{2i}{\pi}\psi_{0},\qquad E_{A}(\{0\})E_{B}(\{\pi\})u=\langle u,\psi_{0}\rangle\langle\psi_{0},u\rangle u=\Bigl(\frac{2}{\pi}\Bigr)^{2}u,$$ because $\langle\psi_{0},u\rangle=\overline{\langle u,\psi_{0}\rangle}=2i/\pi$, so the product of the two coefficients is $(-2i/\pi)(2i/\pi)=4/\pi^{2}$. Thus $E_{A}(\{0\})E_{B}(\{\pi\})u=(4/\pi^{2})u$ while $E_{B}(\{\pi\})E_{A}(\{0\})u=E_{B}(\{\pi\})u=-(2i/\pi)\psi_{0}$. The vectors $u=1$ and $\psi_{0}=e^{i\pi x}$ are linearly independent in $L^{2}(0,1;\mathbb C)$ (the continuous function $e^{i\pi x}$ is not constant on $(0,1)$), so the two results differ. Therefore $E_{A}(\{0\})E_{B}(\{\pi\})\ne E_{B}(\{\pi\})E_{A}(\{0\})$: the spectral projection-valued measures of $A$ and $B$ do not strongly commute, and the refuted statement fails for this pair. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where the core identity loses information.** Both operators are the
  differential expression $-iD$ on different self-adjoint domains; the core
  $C^{\infty}_{c}(0,1)$ sees only the action, not the boundary conditions that
  determine the spectra. The core identity $[A,B]u=0$ is therefore not a
  sufficient condition for strong spectral commutation, while its conclusion
  does hold in finite dimensions and, more generally, when the operators are
  bounded everywhere defined.
- **Boundedness is the missing hypothesis.** For bounded everywhere-defined
  self-adjoint operators the commutator identity $AB=BA$ and strong spectral
  commutation are equivalent; the counterexample shows that no such
  equivalence can be asserted for the unbounded operators of the framework,
  which is why [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-strong-spectral-commutation]] is stated
  at the level of projection-valued measures.

items.title: Time is not an observable of the framework: the conditional timescale bound
items.statement:
## Why there is no energy-time Robertson pair

**Time is a parameter, not an observable.** The framework's evolution
postulate P4 assigns to an isolated system a self-adjoint energy operator and
the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH/\hbar)$ with $t$ a real parameter of the curve
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). The framework's
assigned sharp observables are self-adjoint operators with spectral
projection-valued measures and outcome laws
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]); time is not among them:
there is no assigned self-adjoint time operator whose outcome law would enter
the Robertson relation of [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]], and
this page introduces none. Consequently the expression
$\Delta H\,\Delta t$ is not an instance of the Robertson relation, and the
symbol $\Delta t$ has no definition until a timescale constructed from
observables is specified.

## The conditional timescale bound

**What the framework does support.** The graph-domain Ehrenfest theorem
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-graph-domain-ehrenfest-and-timescale]] is a
conditional mathematical statement about a curve
$\psi:I\to H$ that is $C^{1}$ into the graph norm of a self-adjoint $A$, stays
in $D(AK)$ (and in $D(KA)$ where stated), has unit norm and satisfies
$\psi'=-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}K\psi$. Under those hypotheses, with
$f(t):=\langle A\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ and $f'(t_{0})\ne0$, the timescale
$\tau_{A}(t_{0}):=\Delta A(t_{0})/|f'(t_{0})|$ satisfies
$$\Delta K(t_{0})\,\tau_{A}(t_{0})\ge\frac{\hbar}{2}.$$
With $K=H$ the energy and $A$ a bounded or domain-qualified observable, the
Heisenberg picture identifies $f'(t_{0})$ with the derivative of the mean of
the representative observable
([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-picture]]); the spreads
$\Delta A(t_{0})$ and $\Delta K(t_{0})$ are preparation spreads in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and the theorem's clause (d)
records that when $f'(t_{0})=0$ the quotient supplies no timescale at all.

**What is not claimed.** The timescale $\tau_{A}$ depends on the chosen
observable $A$ and on the state: different choices give different numbers, and
no universal "lifetime" or "duration" of the system is defined. No time
operator, no energy-time Robertson inequality, no claim that an energy
uncertainty is a linewidth and no relation such as $\gamma_{E}\approx\hbar\Gamma$
is asserted by P1-P6; such statements require additional model assumptions
(an apparatus or clock model, a decay model or an analytic continuation) that
are outside this page. The heuristic accounts of measurement disturbance in
the literature are not identities of the framework and are not used as
premises here.

## Remarks

- **Relation to the preparation-spread results.** The timescale bound is a
  Robertson-type estimate applied to the pair (energy, chosen observable)
  along a curve; it does not weaken or strengthen the preparation-spread
  relation of [[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]], which concerns a
  single preparation and two observables.
- **No empirical content.** No measured lifetime, linewidth or energy
  uncertainty is recorded here, and no comparison with data is attempted.

items.title: Preparation spread, apparatus resolution and disturbance are different objects
items.statement:
## Three distinct objects

**Preparation spread.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ and a
preparation $\rho$, the spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that the observable and probability postulate assigns to the pair
$(\rho,A)$: it is a property of the preparation and the assigned observable,
computed from the Born law alone, and it exists only under the stated moment
hypotheses. The inequalities of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] concern these spreads and nothing
else.

**Apparatus resolution or error.** A finite-resolution apparatus is modeled in
this category by a declared instrument with effects and an update rule
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]];
clause (iv) of P2 and the ideal conditional measurement postulate P3 in the
readings of [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]). Whether a
declared effect family approximates a target observable, and by how much, is a
property of the chosen instrument: the postulates do not attach a universal
error parameter to a sharp observable, and the effects alone do not determine
the update ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]).

**Disturbance.** The state change produced by a measurement is likewise part
of the declared instrument: for the framework's declared ideal sharp
measurement the conditional and discarded-outcome updates are specified in
[[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]], and
they are idealizations, not claims about every apparatus. The framework's
postulates assign no universal disturbance to "a measurement of position" as
such.

## What is and is not asserted

**No conflation.** The Robertson relation bounds the product of two
preparation spreads; it does not bound an apparatus error, it does not bound a
disturbance, and it is not a statement that measuring one quantity "must"
perturb another by a fixed amount. The heuristic accounts of measurement
intrusion in the literature are accordingly used on this page at most as
motivation: the exact statements are the preparation-spread results, and the
identification of a concrete apparatus with a declared instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**No universal error-disturbance relation is recorded.** This page and the
measurement page contain no theorem of the form "error times disturbance is at
least $\hbar/2$": such a statement would require declared error and
disturbance quantifiers for an instrument and its own proof. What is recorded
here is only the separation of the three objects and the conditional
results actually proved on the two pages.

## Remarks

- **Why the distinction is load-bearing.** An experiment that reports a finite
  resolution, a detection efficiency or a background model is reporting
  apparatus properties; a preparation spread is a model quantity of the state
  and the assigned observable. Agreement of a measured histogram with a
  predicted distribution tests the combined preparation, apparatus and
  observable identification, not the inequality alone.
- **Disturbance is model-dependent.** Two declared instruments with the same
  outcome effects can have different updates and hence different disturbances,
  as [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]
  records; a disturbance claim must therefore name its instrument.

items.physical_scope: A scope and reading remark separating three notions on the uncertainty and compatibility page and the measurement page of the category: the preparation spread of an outcome law, the resolution or error of a declared apparatus, and the disturbance of the preparation produced by a measurement. The remark records that the framework's postulates define the first through the Born law and the second and third only through declared instruments and apparatus models, and that no universal error-disturbance relation, no universal disturbance bound and no empirical result is asserted. It proves nothing itself.

items.title: What the examples companion records and what it does not
items.statement:
## What the companion contains

**One exact model computation.** [[ex-nrqm-uncertainty-gaussian-minimum-spread]]
computes the position and momentum densities and spreads of the Gaussian
family in the spinless massive model and verifies that the product equals
$\hbar/2$ with the centered vectors linearly dependent and their pairing
purely imaginary, realizing the equality case of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-position-momentum-relation]]. It is a statement about
one family of preparations of the model; it contains no dynamics, no detection
model and no measured number, and it does not characterize all equality
states.

**One finite internal-factor deduction.**
[[texp-nrqm-uncertainty-spin-half-incompatibility]] derives the spread
identity $\sum_{i}(\Delta S_{i})^{2}=3\hbar^{2}/4-|\langle\mathbf S\rangle|^{2}$
for the spin-$\tfrac12$ internal factor, the lower bound $\hbar^{2}/2$, the
failure of spectral compatibility for every pair of components, and the
saturation of the Robertson bound in the $S_{z}$ eigenstates. It is a
conditional deduction inside the model's internal factor; it asserts no
Stern-Gerlach apparatus, no dynamics and no measurement.

**One purely mathematical counterexample.**
[[cex-nrqm-uncertainty-commutator-zero-on-a-core-is-not-spectral-compatibility]]
is a statement of pure mathematics about two self-adjoint extensions of the
interval momentum operator: it refutes the implication from a commutator
identity on a dense core to strong spectral commutation. It carries no
physical premise and makes no physical claim.

**Two scope remarks.** [[rem-nrqm-uncertainty-energy-time-caveat]] records
that time is a parameter and not an observable, so no energy-time Robertson
pair exists here and only the conditional timescale bound is available;
[[rem-nrqm-uncertainty-error-disturbance-distinction]] separates preparation
spread, apparatus resolution and disturbance. Both are readings of other
items, not new theorems.

## What it does not contain

**No experiment and no data.** The companion records no preparation
procedure, apparatus, calibration, trial count, count rate, histogram,
uncertainty budget or statistical analysis, and it uses no empirical premise.
Every quantity computed here is a model quantity. Any comparison with data
would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions through the
identification of a preparation and an apparatus with the model's objects, a
tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus
postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), and would
not turn the conditional results into unconditional statements about nature.

**No universal claims.** The Gaussian family is not all preparations; the
spin deduction concerns the internal factor of the model; the counterexample
concerns two specific operators. In particular the companion does not claim
that every state attaining $\hbar/2$ is Gaussian, that every pair of
incompatible components excludes all forms of joint measurement, or that the
timescale bound is a universal energy-time relation.

## Remarks

- **Reading order.** The mathematical items precede the model computations on
  the main page; the companion consumes the main page's items and adds no new
  supplier to them.
- **Status.** As everywhere in this category, agreement of the conditional
  predictions with a laboratory result would be evidence for the combined
  model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework; the companion
  reports no such result.
